glosses: uppity, haughty, arrogant, proud as a peacock (having excessive pride)

examples.text: Москва Онегина встречает // Своей спесивой суетой, // Своими девами прельщает, // Стерляжьей потчует ухой...
“Donʼt nobody want to see a black man look like you walkinʼ proud as a peacock. Like you ainʼt got a lick of fear in you.”

glosses: Having excessive pride in oneself, often with contempt or disrespect for others.

examples.text: The demand to be loved is the greatest of all arrogant presumptions.
Call me a braggart, call me arrogant. People at ABC (and elsewhere) have called me worse. But when you need the job done on deadline, you’ll call me.

glosses: Conveying in demeanour the assumption of superiority; disdainful, supercilious.

examples.text: How meek and shrunken did that haughty Tarmac become as it slunk by the wide circle of asphalt of the yellow sort, that was loosely strewn before the great iron gates of Lady Hall as a forerunner of the consideration that awaited the guests of Rupert, Earl of Kare, […].

glosses: Presumptuous, above oneself, self-important; arrogant, snobbish, haughty.

examples.text: "Hit wuz wunner dese yer uppity little Jack Sparrers, I speck," said the old man; "dey wuz allers bodder'n' longer udder fokes's bizness

examples.text: And the Yankees are very upset because so many uppity darkies have been killed recently.

glosses: In which the ball is hit into the air, with the chance of being caught.

examples.text: Six runs were still required, and an uppish stroke by the new arrival secured two of them.

examples.text: Da kommt er wieder, der hochmütige Benno.

examples.text: „Anzug trägt er, weißes Hemd, Krawatte, staubfreifein ist er vom gezogenen Scheitel bis zur Budapester Sohle. Junkerhaft, jawohl, so sieht er aus, schnöselig und herrenreiterlich.“
